subtitle: Snoopy's flying fantasy becomes an arcade dogfight

body: Snoopy Flying Ace is Smart Bomb Interactive's Xbox Live Arcade flight-combat game, released on 2 June 2010. It places the Peanuts cast inside a stylised First World War setting, with Snoopy facing the Red Baron and his Flying Circus. Biplanes and triplanes become the means of fast, accessible aerial contests rather than a detailed simulation of historical flying. The player performs evasive manoeuvres, pursues opponents and selects weapons while the familiar characters give the fighting an immediately recognisable comic identity. Two players can also take the entire campaign on together through split-screen cooperation.

Aircraft can be customised visually and equipped with additional weapons, including missiles, floating mines and an electromagnetic blast. Barrel rolls and other acrobatic manoeuvres help change direction or escape an attack. Flying into a stationary turret provides another position from which to join the fight. The player therefore reads the space for useful equipment and angles as well as nearby enemies. After respawning, weapons can be changed to suit a different approach, making another attempt an opportunity to alter the tools brought into the same crowded section of sky.

Online modes supported up to sixteen players, from conventional dogfights to Pigskin, an airborne ball game whose scoring depends on passing between aircraft. Peanuts characters, costumes and Xbox avatars gave players several ways to personalise their pilots. Successful streaks could even bring Woodstock onto the plane to attack enemies behind it. Reviews praised the amount of content and the polished arcade action. Snoopy Flying Ace makes the licence useful through a clear fantasy already associated with its hero, turning the imagined Flying Ace into a coherent flight game with room for cooperative and competitive play.
